page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7a.8xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor and an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7T83 processor. The instance features 32 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. It is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The CPU operates at a base speed of 2.55 GHz and incorporates a cache hierarchy consisting of 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on external storage options and network-attached resources. Network connectivity is supported by an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data indicates that the ecs.g7a.8xlarge delivers strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% on stress-ng tests. Multi-core CPU performance and overall Passmark CPU scores fall within the average tier. Memory performance is mixed; while the Passmark memory score is strong, placing in the top 25%, uncached large-block memory write bandwidth is weak, registering in the bottom 25% at 18.93 GB/sec. Conversely, cached small-block read bandwidth remains average at 2068.83 GB/sec. For language model workloads, the instance demonstrates strong text generation speeds for small 135M models, though prompt processing and medium 7B model execution remain in the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and balanced resource density make this instance suitable for workloads requiring consistent compute availability without the premium of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. The lack of bundled local storage requires users to factor in the cost of network storage. The instance is suited for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, software compilation, database operations, and moderate-scale text processing or small-model language inference.
